claim: The widely-quoted 8.8-year median YouTube channel lifespan is not a median lifespan: CreatorMap defines it as the median age at last upload among channels that have ALREADY gone dark, computed on a cohort that by construction only contains channels that survived long enough to reach 10,000 subscribers by 2019.
stance_target: The claim that the typical YouTube channel lasts about 8.8 years
scope_conditions: CreatorMap, May 2026; the sampling frame mechanically excludes channels that died young, which is why the study can report that only 3.8% of dormant channels went dark within two years; this is left-truncation plus survivorship selection, and the figure cannot be read as the lifespan of a newly started channel
quoted_support: Of all the channels in our dataset that have gone inactive, the single most common age at last upload is 8 to 9 years. The median sits at 8.8 years, with the middle 50% of channels falling between roughly 6 and 12 years.
numbers: modal age 8-9 years (10.1% of dormant channels)
only 3.8% went dark within first 2 years

claim: The CreatorMap half-life article states its sample is 105,891 independent channels while its own page title claims 97,601, and its age-at-death distribution is computed on the identical 40,379 dormant-channel count reported for the separate 97,601-channel survival study.
stance_target: The internal consistency of the CreatorMap creator-longevity dataset
scope_conditions: Page title versus body text of the same article, fetched 27 July 2026
quoted_support: We analyzed 105,891 independent YouTube channels. One question: how long do they actually last?
numbers: 40,379 dormant channels reused across both studies

claim: CreatorMap reports annual channel mortality rising from 3.1 per 1,000 alive channels in 2016 to 41.7 (2019), 57.4 (2022), 76.5 (2023), 104.1 (2024) and 161.6 (2025), a near-tripling in three years, alongside a monthly going-dark rate of 2.36% by September 2025.
stance_target: Creator attrition is accelerating, so older cohort statistics understate the current risk of quitting
scope_conditions: Vendor dataset, single May 2026 snapshot; the rate is measured against channels alive at the start of each year, which the study says controls for cohort size; because inactivity is judged from one snapshot, the most recent years cannot yet be corrected for channels that later resume posting, biasing 2024-2025 rates upward
quoted_support: The rate has nearly tripled since 2022 alone. Channels created in 2012 and channels created in 2019 are both dying at higher per-capita rates in 2024-2025 than in any prior year.

claim: Median channel lifespan in the CreatorMap data varies by four years across content genres, from 7.45 years for People & Blogs to 11.49 years for Nonprofits & Activism, with personal-vlog and general-entertainment formats the shortest-lived.
stance_target: Attrition risk is systematically higher in the low-barrier, high-volume content categories most new creators enter
scope_conditions: 15 content categories, CreatorMap dataset May 2026; inherits the same left-truncated cohort as the 8.8-year median, so genre figures are usable as relative rankings but not as absolute lifespans
quoted_support: Deviation from overall median (8.8y). Spread: People & Blogs (7.45y) to Nonprofits & Activism (11.49y).

claim: CreatorMap's cohort curves show the 2018 creation cohort reaching 50% attrition at age 7, the earliest of any tracked cohort, while the 2012-2017 cohorts still had more than half of channels posting as of mid-2026.
stance_target: Newer creator cohorts face faster attrition than the cohorts that established the platform's success narratives
scope_conditions: CreatorMap, May 2026; the article concedes the 2019-2021 cohorts are too young for firm conclusions; this is the only source in the batch that explicitly acknowledges right-censoring in its survival calculations
quoted_support: Channels classified as active or low-engagement as of May 2026 are treated as right-censored observations in all survival calculations.
numbers: 1.8 years earlier than the overall median
